history.period: Present structure 1809; site ancient (mentioned in 15th-century Manasara Bhashan and 17th-century Kavi Kankan Chandi)
history.summary: Kalighat Kali Temple in Kalighat, Kolkata is the famous Shakti Peetha where the toes of Sati's right foot fell; the name 'Kolkata' is widely believed to derive from 'Kalighat'. The temple stood on the old course of the Hooghly (the Kalighat ghat sacred to Kali) and now lies on the Adi Ganga canal. Believed to date from the time of Chandragupta II; a small temple was built by King Manasingha in the early 16th century, and the present hut-shaped (aatchala/Bengal-style) structure was completed in 1809 under Sabarna Roy Chowdhury patronage (construction began 1798). It is one of the four main Shakti Peethas of India (with Kamakhya, Tara Devi and Bimala). The sanctum is accompanied by the large Nat Mandir congregation hall, a Shiva temple (Nakuleshwar Mahadev) to the north-east, a Radha-Krishna shrine, and the sacred Kundupukur tank whose water is said to bless childless couples. IDENTITY: CONFIRMED — the world-famous Kolkata Kali temple. Note: sources give variant timings; ownership is disputed between the Chowdhurys of Banisha and the Haldar family.

name: Kalighat Kali Temple
town_description: Kolkata, capital of West Bengal on the east bank of the Hooghly, is India's cultural capital and a major metropolis. Kalighat in South Kolkata is the temple quarter built around the shrine, on the banks of the Adi Ganga canal.

travel.airport: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport (~20 km)
travel.railway: Kolkata Railway Station ~13 km; nearest metro stations Jatin Das Park (northern exit) and Kalighat (southern exit); buses and trams from all parts of the city
travel.road: Kali Temple Road, Kalighat, Kolkata 700026 — in South Kolkata, easily reached by metro, bus or taxi

visitor_information.best_time: October–March; visit early morning (6–8 AM) or on Wednesday/Thursday to avoid peak crowds (Tuesdays, Saturdays and festival days are extremely crowded)
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM–2:00 PM and 5:00 PM–10:30 PM (closed 2–5 PM for bhog); closes at 11:30 PM on Saturdays and Sundays per one source — timings vary slightly by source (verify)
